anomalies.observed: On the BMI088 (U5) I2C interface the clock line is not connected to the SCL pin: CSB2 (pin 8, the SCL pin in I2C mode) carries a no-connect marker, the I2C1_SCL_NAVC label is wired to the SDA/SDI pin (9), and the I2C1_SDA_NAVC label is wired to the SDO1 address-strap pin (15). Every other device on the same I2C1 bus (U6 TMP100, U7 MPRLS, U8 IIS2MDCTR, U9 EEPROM) correctly places SCL on its SCL pin and SDA on its SDA pin.
anomalies.expected: Per the datasheet and the spec ('BMI088, I2C addr 0x19 (acc) / 0x69 (gyr)'), CSB2/pin 8 must carry I2C1_SCL_NAVC, SDA/SDI/pin 9 must carry I2C1_SDA_NAVC, and SDO1/pin 15 must be strapped high (to +3.3V) to set the 0x19 accelerometer address. The drawing's pin 8 floating, SCL on the data pin and SDA on the address pin makes the IMU unaddressable and breaks the bus.

evidence.quote: NAVC Peripherals, U5 BMI088 left pins: 7 PS=+3.3V, 14 CSB1=+3.3V, 8 CSB2=x, 9 SDA/SDI=I2C1_SCL_NAVC, 15 SDO1=I2C1_SDA_NAVC, 10 SDO2=+3.3V
IMU (accel + gyro) | NAVCPeripherals | Bosch BMI088, I2C addr 0x19 (acc) / 0x69 (gyr)

anomalies.impact: The accelerometer/gyroscope cannot communicate over I2C (no clock to the device, data line on the wrong pin, and the 0x19 address strap is driven by the SDA bus instead of tied high). The navigation computer loses its primary inertial sensor, so attitude/state estimation and the whole flight-control function fail.

parsed.summary: The power stage, FCC/NAVC MCUs, sensors, regulators, USB-UART bridges and the documented barometer RESET/EOC pin swap all match the specification; the one deviation I can read off the drawing is the BMI088 I2C interface, whose SCL/SDA lines are connected to the wrong pins (SCL pin CSB2 left floating, SCL net on the SDA pin, SDA net on the SDO1 address strap), which would render the IMU unreachable.
